title: Contracted powers of a Zariski torsor form an extension
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and G an abelian sheaf on the small Zariski site X_{\mathrm{Zar}} [def-sc-zariski-site]. For a G-torsor T [def-sc-gm-torsor], let E be the sheaf coproduct over n\in\mathbf Z of the contracted powers T^{\otimes n} of [lem-sc-zariski-contracted-power-torsor]. The canonical torsor isomorphisms T^{\otimes m}\wedge T^{\otimes n}\cong T^{\otimes(m+n)} induce an abelian-sheaf structure on E. The exponent map E\to\mathbf Z_X is a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology] 0\to G\to E\to\mathbf Z_X\to0, and its fibre over 1 is canonically T.

source.place: Lemma 02FQ (cohomology-lemma-torsors-h1), construction of the extension by contracted powers

proof.text: Form the sheaf coproduct E=\coprod_{n\in\mathbf Z}T^{\otimes n}, using the integer powers of [lem-sc-zariski-contracted-power-torsor]. A local section of E is locally in one summand. For local sections a of degree m and b of degree n, define a+b=\mu_{m,n}([a,b]), where [a,b] is their class in the contracted product defined by [lem-sc-torsor-h1]; these local formulas agree under restriction and glue to addition on E. The zero is 0 in the degree-zero summand G. For a local section a of degree n, the torsor isomorphism \mu_{n,-n}:T^{\otimes n}\wedge T^{\otimes(-n)}\cong G gives the unique local section a' of T^{\otimes(-n)} for which \mu_{n,-n}([a,a'])=0; define -a=a'. The unit, associativity and commutativity laws, and the inverse identity, follow from the unital, associative and commutative \mu_{m,n} and their inverse-power pairing in [lem-sc-zariski-contracted-power-torsor].

source.place: Worker's argument from the contracted-product operation; Stacks 02FQ does not construct E by contracted powers

proof.text: Define p:E\to\mathbf Z_X by sending the summand T^{\otimes n} to n. It is a homomorphism because the maps \mu_{m,n} add degrees [lem-sc-zariski-contracted-power-torsor]. Each power is a torsor by the same node, hence locally nonempty by [def-sc-gm-torsor], so p is locally surjective and therefore an epimorphism of sheaves. On local sections, the kernel consists precisely of the degree-zero summand T^{\otimes0}=G; its inclusion identifies G with ker(p). Thus 0\to G\to E\xrightarrow{p}\mathbf Z_X\to0 is short exact in abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology].

proof.text: The fibre of p over the global section 1 consists exactly of the degree-one summand T^{\otimes1}, which is T by [lem-sc-zariski-contracted-power-torsor]. Addition by the degree-zero summand G is the original torsor action by its unit constraint, so this fibre is canonically T.
